findings.title: API Key Exposed in Error Messages and Logs
findings.description: CEREBRAS_API_KEY is loaded into memory without proper isolation. Vulnerable to stack trace exposure, HTTP header logging, error report leakage, and heap dumps.
findings.vulnerable_code: const apiKey = process.env.CEREBRAS_API_KEY; const response = await fetch(..., { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}` } })
attack_vectors: Stack trace exposure in error handlers
HTTP header logging in proxies/middleware
Error report services (Sentry, Rollbar)
Process memory inspection (gcore, gdb)
Heap dumps in monitoring tools
findings.business_impact: Attacker gains access to Cerebras API, can make unlimited API calls, potential account compromise, significant financial loss

steps: Implement masked logging utility for sensitive data
Wrap API calls with error isolation
Add secret scanning in pre-commit hooks
Use environment variables, never log them
Implement structured logging without key/value exposure

findings.title: Missing Rate Limiting on Expensive API Calls
findings.description: No rate limiting, retry limits, or token budgeting on Cerebras API calls. Attacker can trigger DoS via excessive API calls, exhaust quota, cause financial loss.
findings.vulnerable_code: const response = await fetch('https://api.cerebras.ai/v1/chat/completions', { /* no rate limit */ })
attack_vectors: Denial of Wallet: Submit 1000 tasks triggering API calls
Account Lockout: Exceed rate limits, blocking legitimate requests
Cost Explosion: Each call costs money; budget-unaware
Token Exhaustion: No quota tracking
findings.business_impact: Uncontrolled API costs (potentially thousands of dollars), service unavailability, quota lockout preventing legitimate use

steps: Use p-queue or similar queue library for concurrency control
Implement daily token budget tracking
Set rate limits: max 10 requests/minute (configurable)
Add timeout handling (30s default)
Track token usage per request and enforce budget

findings.title: Missing HTTPS Certificate Validation
findings.description: No explicit HTTPS certificate validation or pinning for Cerebras API. Vulnerable to MITM attacks if client environment is compromised.
attack_vectors: Man-in-the-middle attack: Intercept API calls, steal API key and prompts
Certificate spoofing: Impersonate Cerebras API
Traffic inspection: Proxy can log all requests/responses
findings.business_impact: Complete API key compromise, task data exfiltration, ability to impersonate legitimate API calls

steps: Create HTTPS agent with certificate pinning
Specify minimum TLS version 1.2
Pin Cerebras certificate authority
Disable older TLS versions
Test certificate validation with proxy

findings.title: Health Check Endpoint Exposes Internal Details
findings.description: Health check exposes internal configuration details (API key format, database paths, error messages) to unauthenticated users. Enables reconnaissance attacks.
findings.vulnerable_code: return { message: 'RuVector API key not configured', details: { apiKeyConfigured: false } }
attack_vectors: API key format enumeration: Reveals key starts with 'rv_'
Path disclosure: Exposes /var/lib/postgresql/data
Configuration probing: Attacker learns what's missing
findings.business_impact: Information leakage enables targeted attacks, helps attackers understand system architecture

steps: Return generic messages to unauthenticated users
Don't expose database paths or key format hints
Require authentication for detailed health checks
Log internal details to server logs only

findings.title: Prometheus Metrics Endpoint Exposes Sensitive Information
findings.description: Metrics endpoint is publicly accessible (no authentication) and exposes metrics that reveal system behavior and business intelligence (task pass rates, escalation patterns, query latencies).
attack_vectors: Business intelligence gathering: Learn task success/failure rates
System mapping: Understand architecture via latency patterns
Escalation pattern analysis: Detect quality issues
findings.business_impact: Competitive intelligence leakage, helps attackers plan attacks based on system performance patterns

steps: Require OPERATOR+ role for /metrics endpoint
Implement request rate limiting (100 req/min)
Aggregate sensitive metrics (no per-model details)
Create separate admin endpoint with detailed metrics

findings.title: Authentication Middleware Not Enforced Globally
findings.description: Authentication middleware exists but is not applied globally. Endpoints may be accessible without authentication if middleware is not explicitly attached. Dev mode enables ADMIN access without credentials if NODE_ENV not set.
findings.vulnerable_code: if (authConfig.devMode) { return { role: Role.ADMIN, ... } }  // Dev mode gives free ADMIN!
attack_vectors: Unauthenticated endpoint access: Endpoints without explicit auth middleware
Dev mode bypass: If NODE_ENV not explicitly set to production
Default to ADMIN role: Dev mode gives full system access
findings.business_impact: Complete system compromise if dev mode enabled in production, unauthorized access to collections and data

steps: Apply auth middleware globally to all endpoints
Require explicit opt-in for dev mode: ALLOW_DEV_MODE=true
Explicitly set NODE_ENV=production
Define public endpoints (only /health with limited info)
Add request logging for all accesses

findings.title: Service-to-Service Auth Uses Plaintext Secrets
findings.description: Service secrets stored in environment variables and compared using string equality (timing attack vulnerable). Secrets visible via 'ps aux' and should use timing-safe comparison.
findings.vulnerable_code: if (!expectedSecret || serviceSecret !== expectedSecret) return null;  // Timing attack!
attack_vectors: Timing attack: Character-by-character comparison reveals secret length/content
Environment variable exposure: Secrets visible via ps aux, /proc filesystem
No secret rotation: Stored in env vars indefinitely
findings.business_impact: Service-to-service authentication bypass, attackers can impersonate services

steps: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual() for secret comparison
Move secrets to Docker Secrets (/run/secrets/)
Implement secret rotation policy (30-day rotation)
Add audit logging for service authentication

findings.deployment: Use Docker secrets: docker secret create service_secret_ruvector <secret>

findings.title: Audit Log Not Persisted (In-Memory Only)
findings.description: Audit logs stored in-memory only. Lost on process restart. Violates compliance requirements (GDPR, SOC 2) for audit trail retention.
findings.vulnerable_code: auditLog.push(entry); if (auditLog.length > 10000) { auditLog.shift(); }  // Loses old logs!
attack_vectors: Data loss: Audit logs discarded on restart
No accountability: Can't investigate past incidents
Compliance violation: GDPR Article 32 requires record keeping
findings.business_impact: Loss of audit trail, inability to investigate security incidents, compliance violations

steps: Migrate audit logs to PostgreSQL
Create audit table with proper indexing
Implement database persistence with fallback to file
Add query functions for audit log retrieval
Set retention policy (90-365 days)

findings.title: Missing Configuration Validation at Startup
findings.description: No validation of required environment variables at application startup. Missing or invalid configuration discovered at first use, causing runtime errors.
attack_vectors: Silent failures: System starts without required config
Error-time discovery: Errors only appear during first API call
Misconfiguration: Admin sets wrong database URL, discovered late
findings.business_impact: Operational issues, late discovery of configuration problems, downtime during deployment

steps: Create validation function for all required env vars
Check at application startup before listening
Validate database URL format
Check JWT secret length (32+ characters)
Verify directory permissions (RUVECTOR_DB_PATH)

findings.title: Missing SQL Injection Protection (If Using Database)
findings.description: If system uses SQL queries, ensure parameterized queries are used everywhere. Audit log migration must use prepared statements.
findings.vulnerable_code: // Example of vulnerable code (if it existed) const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${userId}`
attack_vectors: SQL injection: Attacker modifies query via input parameters
Data exfiltration: Unauthorized access to database records
Data manipulation: Modify or delete audit logs
findings.business_impact: Complete database compromise, data theft, audit trail manipulation

steps: Use parameterized queries for all SQL
Use ORM or query builder (TypeORM, Knex) instead of raw SQL
Validate input types before queries
Use prepared statements with binding
Audit all existing queries for injection vulnerabilities
remediation.code_example: // Correct: Prepared statement with parameterized query
remediation.correct_code: await pool.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1', [userId])

affected_files: All database interaction code (to be audited)

findings.title: Incomplete Error Handling (May Expose Details)
findings.description: Error handlers may expose stack traces, internal file paths, or configuration details to clients. Need consistent error response pattern.
findings.vulnerable_code: throw new Error(`Failed to load config from ${configPath}: ${error.message}`)
attack_vectors: Stack trace leakage: Full stack traces sent to clients
Path disclosure: Internal file paths exposed
Error chaining: Original error details propagated
findings.business_impact: Information leakage, helps attackers understand system architecture and find exploitable paths

steps: Create consistent error response format
Log full error details server-side only
Send generic error messages to clients
Use error IDs for traceability
Never expose file paths or config details

server_logging.error: Full stack trace and context logged with traceId

findings.title: Missing Security Best Practices Documentation
findings.description: No documented security guidelines for developers. Need runbook for secure operations, incident response, and deployment procedures.
findings.impact: Developers may make insecure decisions without guidance

steps: Create SECURITY.md with guidelines
Document how to report security issues
Create incident response playbook
Document secure deployment checklist
Add security training links for team

findings.title: Missing Graceful Shutdown with Cleanup
findings.description: Application may not properly close database connections or flush audit logs on shutdown. Could cause data loss.
findings.impact: Potential data loss, incomplete audit logs on crash

steps: Add signal handlers for SIGTERM and SIGINT
Gracefully close database connections
Flush pending audit logs
Wait for pending requests to complete (timeout 30s)
Exit cleanly with code 0
